title: Diagnostic: weak Must Be an Optional var
hints: ARC sets weak references to `nil` — so they must be optional.
Declare the weak property with a **non-optional** type.
jsBridge: A `weak` reference must be an optional `var`, because ARC sets it to `nil` automatically when the object dies. JS `WeakRef` is similar (`deref()` can return `undefined`), but Swift makes the nil-ing visible in the type.

compass.q: JS `WeakRef.deref()` may return `undefined`. How does Swift's `weak var x: T?` express the same thing in the type?
`weak` vs `unowned`: which one crashes if the object is gone? When is `unowned` justified?
Can a `weak` reference point to a struct? Why not?
`weak var delegate` is idiomatic. What goes wrong if you forget `weak`?
